segments.interpretation: A strictly positive descriptive difference in observed one-hour log returns is tested using the specified aggregate episode proxies. The parent-order account remains a conjecture, not an identified parent-order measurement or causal estimand.
segments.text: Hypothesis: a BTC buying episode carried by unusually many small transactions, with persistent buyer-initiated participation but ordinary total turnover, predicts higher subsequent one-hour BTC returns relative to the whole eligible BTC scope. The mechanism conjectured is persistent execution of sliced parent buy orders: elevated transaction frequency without a proportionate increase in notional turnover may reflect repeated small child orders rather than a single completed block. Two consecutive buyer-dominated bars and upward price progress suggest that liquidity suppliers are allowing prices to adjust rather than fully absorbing demand. Remaining parent-order demand could continue after the reporting delay. Trade fragmentation can also arise from exchange matching, retail activity, or market-maker behavior, so these proxies do not establish parent orders.

segments.interpretation: The outer lag places the episode anchor at b=t-900; its local lag one reads b-d, and baseline lag two places the complete window before both episode bars. Historical reads retain decision cutoff t. Availability evidence 7a7eeb040cf86f182bfacd7952a03bfc46046b6e14f2905836490f12f6706323 covers this exact snapshot and BTC features: every present entry has available_at=s+900. The latest condition dependency b is therefore available at t. For the outcome, the latest dependency t+4*d is available exactly at a=t+5*d, while C_t is available earlier. Thus the inherited later as_of cutoff cannot admit a dependency arriving after a on this snapshot; the exclusive-end cap still applies. Absent and null entries remain missing. This derivation uses the fixed-delay evidence, not historical publication truth, and does not make either decision or outcome-anchor containers additional observations.
segments.text: Timing: let d=900 seconds and b=t-d. Keys represent exclusive complete-bar ends. A raw observation ending s is usable only after s+d, and only if otherwise available. Publication at s+d is an assumption, not proven historical point-in-time truth. At any evaluation anchor a use availability cutoff min(a, 2023-04-01T00:00:00Z minus one second). Assess the condition at t using bars ending b and b-d, never raw features ending t.

segments.interpretation: The predicate at /condition_ast/expression/arg/left/right implements both episode tests against the same complete 16-bar means over b-17*d through b-2*d and the exact simple two-bar price-progress test. The complete-validity composition is at /condition_ast/expression/arg, with identical V copies at /condition_ast/expression/arg/left/left and /condition_ast/expression/arg/right/left/arg. The owned exact projections in dfebc7e3d378cbc928c8a1a149177fe5dd8d730e3cc485f0a1716ea42bbbfaab restrict observed trade counts to nonnegative integers and quote volumes to nonnegative decimals; invalid keyed bars are all-null and nonfinite execution values fail admission. Consequently the complete 18-position mean of N/N equals one exactly when all 16 baseline and both episode counts are present and positive integers. Zero counts create missing division results, not valid zeros. The complete two-position Q/Q identity likewise requires both episode volumes positive. Complete MQ>0 validates baseline completeness and positive mean; individual baseline nonnegativity is supplied by the exact nonnegative-decimal projection, so valid baseline zeros are allowed. Explicit checks enforce B>=0 and B<=Q at both episode bars and positivity of C_b and O_{b-d}. V cannot be true with any required input absent, null, unavailable or invalid. When V is false or unknown the guard returns unknown regardless of a false scientific component. These source-domain dependencies are qualified execution definitions, not a new integer operator or scientific feature certification.
segments.text: Exact condition: write N_s for BTC trade count, Q_s for quote volume, B_s for taker quote volume, and O_s,C_s for open and close. Define baseline means MN=(sum of N_{b-k*d} for k=2,...,17)/16 and MQ=(sum of Q_{b-k*d} for k=2,...,17)/16. Thus the baseline is the 16 exact bars immediately preceding the two-bar episode and excludes both episode bars. The condition is true exactly when, for EACH s in {b-d,b}, N_s >= 2*MN, 0.75*MQ <= Q_s <= 1.25*MQ, and B_s/Q_s >= 0.60, AND C_b/O_{b-d}-1 >= 0.001. Require all inputs finite, episode Q_s>0, baseline Q_s>=0, MQ>0, all trade counts positive integers, and 0<=B_s<=Q_s; both endpoint prices must be positive. No other filters apply.

segments.interpretation: All scientific thresholds and windows retain the original exploratory commitments. The 18-position validity window is the union of the specified 16 baseline and two episode bars, not an altered activity reference. Unit identities in the guard merely test required completeness and positivity on the owned source domains. No threshold is chosen from development outcomes; taker-volume interpretation remains qualified.
segments.text: Rationale for every numeric choice: 16 bars provide a local four-hour activity reference; two consecutive bars require persistence over 30 minutes rather than a single matching burst. Twice baseline transaction count with turnover within 75%-125% of baseline isolates substantially smaller average prints while avoiding a turnover collapse. A 60% taker-buy share requires a meaningful directional majority without implying that every small print is a buy. A 0.1% two-bar rise requires ten basis points of realized upward progress. These are mechanism-motivated exploratory commitments, not thresholds fitted to counts or outcomes. Interpreting taker quote volume as buyer-initiated turnover remains subject to feature certification.

segments.interpretation: At future anchor t+5*900, numerator lag one reads C_{t+4*d} and denominator lag five reads C_t. The program computes exactly 10000 times the natural logarithm of their dimensionless ratio in basis_points, with bounded-math/1.0 outward enclosures, not a simple return or next-bar body. The owned positive-decimal close projection and finite-input admission preserve the positive finite price requirement; invalid keyed closes are null. Exact feature reads require both permitted keys and availability. The horizon must elapse and remain in the declared universe; no April or substitute close is read. C_t is never a decision-condition input or claimed attainable entry quote.
segments.text: Outcome: choose positive integer h=5; evaluate at a=t+5*d. Define Y(t)=10000*ln(C_{t+4*d}/C_t), using BTC closes keyed by exclusive bar ends. This measures the one-hour market log return from t to t+3600 seconds in log basis points. The fifth interval permits the terminal close its assumed publication delay. Both closes must be finite, positive, within the permitted interval and available by the anchor cutoff. C_t is an outcome input, unavailable to the condition at t, not an executable entry price. Raw prices have units USDT/BTC; their ratio is dimensionless.

segments.interpretation: The estimand is mean(Y|C=true,S=true,Y observed) minus mean(Y|S=true,Y observed), with equal rows, positive direction, no nuisance fitting, and whole_scope comparator. segments.text: Comparison: the hypothesized descriptive contrast is strictly positive: equal-row mean Y among condition-true rows minus equal-row mean Y across the whole decision scope with observed Y, including condition-false and condition-unknown rows. This intentionally uses the installed whole-scope benchmark, not a false-only, matched, causal or beta-adjusted comparison. It does not require the conditional return itself to be positive. Include overlapping outcomes without thinning; rows are not independent samples.

Unknown-condition rows remain in scope and contribute to its mean when Y is observed, but never to the conditioned mean.
